verdict_json.summary: The raw_event section reports ransomware-like file renames (rule 92002) on high-criticality Finance workstation HOST-A2 for user E2EA\j.doe, with a parent path of winword.exe but a parent command line of hidden, encoded PowerShell (-nop -w hidden -enc…), which is inconsistent and highly suspicious. The correlations section shows a related Certutil download alert on the same host and user about ten minutes earlier, supporting a multi-stage chain hypothesis. Confidence is capped because the same raw_event marks the alert as synthetic E2E, runbooks and prior_cases are empty, and process IDs, hashes, network addresses, working directory, and full rename/file evidence are listed as missing.
verdict_json.root_cause: Hypothesis only: user or document-driven Word activity on HOST-A2 led to obfuscated PowerShell (encoded command consistent with an IEX/New-Object-style cradle prefix in the provided -enc string), preceded by certutil-based download, culminating in ransomware-like mass renames—while noting the dossier also labels this a synthetic E2E alert, so production compromise is not proven.
recommended_actions: Isolate HOST-A2 from the network pending containment review
Disable or reset E2EA\j.doe credentials and review concurrent sessions
Preserve volatile evidence: memory, Prefetch, PowerShell logs, Sysmon/EDR process tree, recent file rename/extension changes
Hunt for the related certutil download alert artifacts (downloaded path, URL, hash) on HOST-A2
Block and inventory any newly written/renamed files and backup restore options for Finance shares if encryption is confirmed
Treat as synthetic/test only after human confirmation that no live host impact occurred; do not close solely on the synthetic flag
Escalate to IR for ransomware playbook (business impact, backups, blast radius)
